Colour palette chip for a page's maps

Source: R/filter-palette.R
cd_palette_chip.Rd

A filter chip that chooses the colour palette of the maps on a page. It belongs in the bar of map options above the maps (cd_map_options()). The page reads the choice as input$<inputId> and passes it to the map plots, which accept these palette names.

Usage

cd_palette_chip(inputId, i18n, first = "Greens")

Arguments

inputId

The input's id. Inside a module, pass it through the module's ns().

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

first

The palette listed first, and so the one the page opens with: "Greens" (the default), "Blues", "Reds" or "Purples". Any other value leaves the order as it is, with "Greens" first.

Value

The UI as Shiny tags (the chip). Its value, input$<inputId>, is the chosen palette's name.

Details

The choices are four sequential RColorBrewer palettes: "Greens", "Blues", "Reds" and "Purples". The chip starts on its first choice, so first decides which palette a page opens with. This is a plain input, not a module, so there is no server function to call.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cd_map_options(cd_palette_chip(ns("palette"), i18n, first = "Blues"))
} # }
